 ‘God of War’ TV Show: Release Date, Cast and Everything We Know About Prime Video’s Series
 Emma Loggins 
 Founder & Editor-in-Chief · October 30, 2026 · 4 min read 
 Follow 
 Table of Contents When does it come out? 
 Who plays Kratos now? 
 Who else is in the cast? 
 Which games does it adapt? 
 Who is running the show? 
 Update log 
 Prime Video’s God of War has already survived the kind of year most productions never recover from. Cameras rolled in Vancouver in February 2026, its first Kratos tore a bicep during a stunt in June, every finished episode is being reshot, and Dave Bautista stepped into the role in August. Through all of it, the two-season order never wavered. I read that as the loudest signal yet of how much Sony and Amazon are betting on the God of War TV show.
 Streaming home is Prime Video, from Sony Pictures Television, Amazon MGM Studios and PlayStation Productions.
 No release date yet, and Amazon’s own press site lists Season 1 as TBA.
 Ronald D. Moore is the showrunner.
 Dave Bautista plays Kratos, with Callum Vinson as Atreus.
 Two seasons are ordered, both adapting the Norse era of the games.
 Production is based in Vancouver.
 Kratos and Atreus in the 2018 God of War game. (Image: PlayStation) 
 When does it come out?
 Nobody has put a date on it. Amazon MGM Studios’ press site still shows Season 1 with a TBA launch, and neither studio has named a year. The production timeline explains the silence. Filming started in February and stopped after Ryan Hurst’s injury, and Deadline reported that the four episodes already shot would be redone with a new Kratos, with the studios targeting a mid-October restart in Vancouver, as Engadget summarized.
 That effectively resets Season 1 to zero this fall. A 2026 premiere is off the table, and I would treat any specific date floating around for the series as a guess until Prime Video posts one itself.
 Who plays Kratos now?
 Dave Bautista. Hurst, cast in January 2026, tore his bicep filming a stunt in late June and needed surgery, and the studios decided they could not wait out a recovery measured in months. Bautista’s casting was locked in August, which Deadline and CGMagazine both reported. We covered every turn of it here, from the Hurst injury to the confirmed recast .
 I think the swap works in the show’s favor. Bautista spent years as Drax in the Guardians of the Galaxy films, a part built on deadpan menace and buried grief, and that is close to the exact register Kratos lives in. He has also been open about the training, telling fans he was two months out from a Kratos-ready body back in September.
 Who else is in the cast?
 Callum Vinson as Atreus
 Mandy Patinkin as Odin
 Ed Skrein as Baldur
 Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor
 Teresa Palmer as Sif
 Max Parker as Heimdall
 Alastair Duncan as Mimir
 Sonya Walger as Freya
 Danny Woodburn as Brok
 Jeff Gulka as Sindri
 Louis Cunningham as Modi
 Ben Chapple as Magni
 Island Austin as Thrud
 Evelyn Miller as Gna
 Duncan is the name game fans should care about most, since GameSpot notes he is the first actor from the games to carry his role over to the God of War TV show. Skrein is the other piece that matters, and our Baldur casting breakdown lays out why the villain of the 2018 game needs an actor who can be charming and unhinged in the same scene.
 Ed Skrein plays Baldur in Prime Video’s God of War . (Image: FanBolt) 
 Which games does it adapt?
 The Norse era. The series is built on the 2018 God of War and its 2022 sequel God of War Ragnarök , opening with Kratos and Atreus setting out to scatter the ashes of Faye, his wife and the boy’s mother, from the highest peak in the nine realms. The Greek revenge saga that made Kratos famous is backstory, not the template, and that is the right call. The 2018 game is the most character-driven story the franchise has told, and a father learning to talk to his son is a premise that survives the jump to television far better than boss fights do.
 Season 2 is already shaping the cast. MP1st reported casting calls for teenage versions of Atreus and Thrud, which tracks with the multi-year time jump between the two games, as Tech Times laid out. Treat that as reported rather than announced, since Prime Video has not confirmed it.
 Who is running the show?
 Ronald D. Moore took over as writer, showrunner and executive producer in October 2024, after the original team of Rafe Judkins, Mark Fergus and Hawk Ostby exited when the studios chose a different direction. Moore’s Tall Ship Productions produces alongside Sony Pictures Television, Amazon MGM Studios and PlayStation Productions. Frederick E.O. Toye directs the first two episodes.
 Moore is the reason I am not worried about the series despite the chaos. He turned Battlestar Galactica into a serious drama about grief and violence wearing a genre costume, and that is precisely the trick this adaptation has to pull off. Prime Video’s first look image back in February showed the tone was already right. Now it just needs its Kratos back on camera.
 Update log
 October 23, 2026. Guide launched with the Bautista recast, the reshoot of the first four episodes, the full announced cast, and the Season 2 casting reports. Release date still TBA.
